Bottom line: Comparing passive conductive mesh, clear disc pens, and fine-tip capacitive styluses for drawing and word search grids. Compare movement, space, and cleaning needs; try what you own for 5 minutes before shopping.

While fingers work well for tapping large cards in Klondike, games with drawing inputs or detailed grids—such as Pass the Picture, Word Search, and Nonogram—benefit significantly from the precision of a stylus.

A stylus prevents your finger from blocking the line you are drawing and provides a natural pen-and-paper feel.

Stylus types compared

Passive Conductive Mesh Styluses. These work on any capacitive touchscreen without batteries, pairing, or charging. Micro-knit conductive fiber tips glide smoothly across glass without sticking.

Precision Disc Styluses. These feature a clear plastic disc around a fine ballpoint tip, allowing you to see exactly where your line begins while maintaining electrical contact with the screen.

Active Pens (Apple Pencil, S Pen). Supported by specific tablet models, active styluses offer sub-pixel precision and palm rejection.

Alternatives already nearby

If you prefer using your fingers, keeping your screen clean with a microfiber cloth drastically reduces friction when dragging word paths in Word Search.
